chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Mu'awiya said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Locusts are on the side of the road, and people are praying (in a state of Ihram); what should they do?' He said: 'They should avoid them as much as they can.' I said: 'If they kill some of them, is there anything upon them?' He said: 'There is nothing upon them.' The meaning in this narration is what has been clarified, that they kill them in a manner in which they cannot avoid them, so no expiation is required of them, and this adds to the clarification.'

key_terms.يُحرِمُونَ: They are in a state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing locusts while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies that the prohibition of killing specific animals in Ihram does not extend to locusts, as they are not considered 'game' (sayr) in the same juristic sense. The scholar highlights that even if killing occurs during the active process of avoidance, no expiation is due, emphasizing the principle of ease for the pilgrim when dealing with common pests. This ruling distinguishes locusts from larger game animals, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the scope of Ihram restrictions.
